# Foreman · dsh-agent-foreman

> Parent agent dispatches, sub-agents do the work, the parent reviews.
> No preset roles, no scripte
d phases: **you decide who works and with which model**.
Chinese docs: README.zh.md · Install / upgrade
**Latest release: v0.4.1 (2026-11-07)** — re-verified against DSH 0.2.2-rc.1 with forward-compatible
provider discovery.
## The problem

DSH's built-in Agent Team lets you give each teammate a name and a prompt — but **not a model**.
Rea

l work is mixed: some of it needs an expensive model, some of it is a two-line edit.
Inheriting the
parent's model for every pair of hands is both slow and expensive.
Foreman splits it in two:

- **Contractors** — the crew you define in the settings page, named by trade like a real
constructio

n site: 力工 (laborer — does the business work) and, optionally, 安全员 (safety officer
— reviews and rej

ects). The foreman itself is the parent agent: it splits the work and signs off,
and is never in the

roster. Want specialties? **Hire several instances** (力工 · frontend,
力工 · render), each with its ow

n model and **its own prompt** (the Edit prompt button),
and its own ordinary-mode concurrency cap (

default 1). Native team mode always serializes
one member’s inbox; use additional members for indepe
ndent parallel work. That prompt is prepended to every order the contractor receives. **The minimal

setup
is a single 力工.**
- **Orders** — the work the parent agent splits out. Each order carries a ta

sk and acceptance
criteria, and may name a contractor or leave it out to be picked by live load (bus

y contractors
are skipped, the least loaded one wins, and a rotation cursor breaks ties — cross-sess

tractors
are skipped, the least loaded one wins, and a rotation cursor breaks ties — cross-session).

The parent only splits work and reviews results. Everything in between happens in isolated child
ses
sions, and the products come back as one shared board.
## Install
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Manual (dev) install:

1. Copy the whole directory to `<profile>/node_modules/dsh-agent-foreman`
2. Add `"dsh-agent-foreman

"` to `dsh.profile.bundles` in `<profile>/package.json`
3. Restart DSH
Then open **Settings → 包工头** and add contractors.
## Usage

Type `/foreman` (registered at runtime through `ctx.skills.register()`) followed by the work:
`/fore

man extract GraphBlocked into shared logic; add regression tests`. Semicolons or newlines
split orde

rs. The skill body walks the parent through roster → split → one dispatch → review, so no
standing s
ystem prompt is needed.
| Tool | Purpose |
| `foreman_roster` | List contractors with route, prompt length, concurrency cap, and the current po

licy |
| `foreman_dispatch` | Dispatch a batch of orders, wait for all of them, return the board |
|

`foreman_review` | Pass / fail each order; a failed one is re-dispatched with feedback |
| `foreman
_status` | Re-read a board; omit `runId` for the latest one in this session |
### Where members show up

**Settings → 包工头 → 实时工地** is a polling board over `api/live`: whether the foreman is
working, each c

ontractor's role and model, and every order's status / dependencies / error /
artifact path for the
current round. It pauses itself while the page is hidden.

The important part: the board shows both the **declared model** (what the roster says) and the
**act

ual model** (read back from the child session's header). When they differ the row is
flagged — that

is the direct answer to "which model is actually running this order". In team
mode the actual model
comes from the host's `listMembers()` model field.

In team mode a contractor **is** a real Agent Teams member, so the native `Agent Teams` button in
th
e session header lists them too. The settings page keeps the full roster editor.
Roster notes:

- A contractor is a name, an optional role (a lightweight trade label for routing, not a fixed
perso

na), an optional prompt, a provider, a model, an effort level and a concurrency cap.
**Leave the pro

vider on "follow the current session" and the child simply runs on whatever model
the parent session

is using.**
- To use a different model: pick the provider first — **the model dropdown is derived f

rom it** and
only lists that provider's models (providers with no models never show up).
- Settings

page collapses policy behind "派单策略". Each contractor has a responsive group with
readable model/effo

rt controls, a full configured-route summary and an Edit prompt button.
The header popover stays ins
ide the viewport and distinguishes configured from observed models.
### The roster *is* the whitelist

The host keeps its own **subagent model whitelist** (`subagent-model-selection`), which decides
whic

h provider/model routes child agents may use. That list and the roster are configured
separately, so

when they drift apart the roster says `trae` while the children quietly run
something else — with n

apart the roster says `trae` while the children quietly run
something else — with no error anywhere.

This plugin folds that into one place: **every enabled contractor with an explicit provider+model
is
collected into the host whitelist automatically.** You only maintain the roster.

- Synced once at plugin startup, again after saving the roster, and on demand via
`POST /api/whiteli

st/sync`.
- If no contractor declares an explicit route (all "follow the current session"), the host

configuration is left untouched — an empty list makes the host throw.
- Applies to **new sessions o

nly**. The host snapshots the whitelist into a session when that
session is first created, so existi

ng sessions keep the old list; open a new session after
changing the roster.
- A failed sync never b

locks dispatch — it only logs. `/api/state` exposes the live `whitelist`
field.
Dispatch notes:

- `orders[].task` **must be self-contained** — the child cannot see the parent's context.
- `orders[

].contractor` accepts a contractor **name or id**, or a `role` trade label; name/id
[该节后续省略]
## Security

- Every HTTP route accepts same-origin, loopback requests only; cross-site calls get 403.
- The rost

er stores provider/model/effort names — never credentials.
- Contractors run in their own child sess
ions and inherit DSH's effective sandbox.
